memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"For seven days eat bread made without yeast and on the seventh day hold a
festival to the LORD. Eat unleavened bread during those seven days; nothing with
yeast in it is to be seen among you, nor shall any yeast be seen anywhere within
your borders." - Ex 13:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God is thorough. Not just no yeast in the bread, but no yeast to be seen in the
house, or anywhere within their borders.

We might think that is excessive. Surely a small jar tucked at the back of a
cupboard would do no harm? But that is precisely the point. Yeast spreads. It
does not stay where you leave it. What is kept "just in case" is what eventually
works through everything.

Jesus used the same picture more than once, warning about the yeast of the
Pharisees, which was hypocrisy (Luke 12:1). Notice what He identified: not
scandalous sin, but the quiet gap between how we appear and what we actually
are. That is the kind of yeast we are most likely to keep in the cupboard.

Here is the balance we must hold. This thoroughness is not a way of earning
God's favour. The blood was applied before any of this was commanded. Israel was
already redeemed. The clearing out came after the rescue, never in order to
secure it.

So we deal seriously with sin, not anxiously. A redeemed person cleaning house,
not a slave trying to buy freedom.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you keeping "just in case" that has no place in a redeemed life?
2. Is there a gap between how you appear and who you actually are?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, search my house and show me what I have quietly kept. Help me to clear it
out as Your child, secure in Your love. Amen.
